evidence.note: After the big rewrite it immediately establishes an aggregate baseline (2/459→376/459, then 95.4%) and repeatedly categorizes failures with grep -oE 'FAIL: [a-z_]+' | sort | uniq -c, separating assert_invalid vs assert_return vs assert_trap — a running reconciliation of what remains rather than a vague sense.

Tracks the aggregate climbing (95.9%→...) and repeatedly re-runs the full categorization after each fix, working the small set of functional assert_return/trap failures one line at a time (conversions L123, f32.nearest L2505, call_indirect trap msg) and confirming each is gone before moving on — detects and closes individual stuck assertions.

Quantifies the remaining gap concretely (1381 assert_invalid failures dominate) and reallocates effort toward the highest-remaining bucket by building a validator, yielding the 99.4% jump — classic effort reallocation to the largest-remaining family.
Catches a regression: the new validator rejects valid modules ('no current module' on block/loop), i.e. a fix in one area broke another; diagnoses block.0.wasm and fixes pop_ctrl, restoring 99.8%.

Maintains a precise shrinking remaining-count ledger to 1.0 across the long tail (69 left → 30 left → 10 global-only → 0), attributing each residual to specific families (simd_align alignment, simd_lane index, global const-expr) and clearing them, never losing the plot.

reasoning: The agent continuously reconciles the aggregate score and per-failure-type/per-file counts after nearly every change, quantifies the remaining gap to 1.0 concretely (198→69→30→10→0), and reallocates effort to the highest-remaining bucket (the 1381 assert_invalid failures → validator), matching the 8 anchor and reaching into 10 territory. It also detects a fix-induced regression (validator breaking valid block modules) and resolves stuck single assertions individually. It falls short of a full 10 only because progress state is re-derived on demand via grep rather than maintained as an explicit persistent done/remaining/blocked ledger, and SIMD families were never tracked as a written checklist.
